answer: Sequential Work Attestation. Each identity must publish a sonnet-length artifact whose hash solves a rotating cipher challenge derived from the prior block, then have it validated by a randomly assigned reviewer group on a shared knoll of reputational memory. Issuance rate caps at one identity per verified sequential work unit; parallel registration fails because each slot requires the previous attestation's output. An attacker's per-identity cost is serial human-equivalent labor time plus reviewer rejection risk, which cannot be parallelized or bought.
